news.text: 3 October saw astrophysicists publish decisive orbital measurements demonstrating the presence of a supermassive **black hole** at the centre of our galaxy, **Sagittarius A***. By tracking the astonishing velocities of nearby stars orbiting the Milky Way's core, researchers proved that millions of solar masses were concentrated in an extraordinarily compact cosmic region. The landmark discovery provided conclusive proof for long-debated gravitational theories, eventually yielding the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physics.

news.text: 9 October saw culinary duo Clarissa Dickson Wright and Jennifer Paterson roar onto **BBC Two** with the debut of *Two Fat Ladies*. Riding a 1930s-style Triumph Thunderbird motorcycle with a Watsonian sidecar, the eccentric cooks traversed the British countryside preparing lavish meals packed with lard, double cream, and unrepentant quantities of **butter**. The show was an immediate smash hit, offering an anarchic rebuke to contemporary healthy eating advice with hearty laughter and liberal splashes of alcohol.
news.youtube: Two Fat Ladies BBC 1996 first episode

news.text: 16 October saw the official publication of the **Cullen Report** into the tragic Dunblane primary school massacre. Led by Lord Cullen, the public inquiry severely criticized police licensing procedures and set out recommendations that led directly to a near-total ban on civilian **handgun ownership** across Great Britain. Backed by the public *Snowdrop Campaign*, the findings prompted Prime Minister John Major's government to draft stringent firearms legislation that permanently reshaped British gun control.

20 October saw the WWF host its first ever Buried Alive match at *In Your House 11* in Indianapolis. **The Undertaker** successfully defeated bitter rival **Mankind** by chokeslamming him into an open grave and burying him in dirt, only to be ambushed by The Executioner, Goldust, Crush and Triple H. The villains proceeded to bury The Undertaker beneath a towering mound of earth, only for a dramatic flash of lightning to strike the grave as the show closed, revealing the Deadman's gloved hand clawing its way back to the surface.

20 October saw Kevin Keegan's **Newcastle United** demolish reigning champions **Manchester United 5–0** in an electrifying Premier League clash at St James' Park. Goals from Darren Peacock, David Ginola, Les Ferdinand and Alan Shearer had already left Alex Ferguson's side shellshocked before Belgian defender Philippe Albert capped the rout with an outrageous 25-yard chip over Peter Schmeichel. Commentator Andy Gray memorably remarked that if the performance was the cake, Albert's chip was the icing.

news.text: 22 October saw the tragic death of **Chelsea FC** vice-chairman and millionaire businessman **Matthew Harding** at the age of 42 in a helicopter crash in Cheshire. Harding, a passionate supporter who had invested heavily in modernising Stamford Bridge and transforming the club's fortunes on the pitch, was returning home from a League Cup tie against Bolton Wanderers. Tributes flooded in from across English football, with Chelsea subsequently naming the new North Stand in his honour.

25 October saw British developer Core Design unleash *Tomb Raider* across European store shelves, making its exclusive debut on the **Sega Saturn**. Starring aristocratic adventurer **Lara Croft**, the game dazzled gamers with fluid acrobatics, complex ancient puzzles, and sweeping three-dimensional environments that redefined action-adventure gaming. The title became an immediate sensation and propelled its digital heroine into a bona fide global cultural icon.
news.youtube: Tomb Raider Sega Saturn 1996 original release

news.text: 26 October saw pop phenomenon the **Spice Girls** secure their second consecutive number one on the UK singles chart with *Say You'll Be There*. Following the enormous summer breakthrough of *Wannabe*, the sleek harmonica-laced pop track proved that **Girl Power** was far more than a one-hit novelty. The accompanying music video, which saw the group dressed as ninja-styled secret agents in the Mojave Desert, received relentless rotation across music television channels.
